title: The Timer That Fell Behind: QTimer Intervals, a Blocked Loop and the Ticks Nobody Counted

questions.question: A repeating 10 ms QTimer is blocked for 100 ms by a slow handler. What happens to the ticks in that time?
options: The timer stops
They are delivered one per period until it catches up
They are all delivered at once afterwards
They are gone: the timer does not queue them, and nothing says so
questions.explanation: The lesson's ticker saw 10 slots go by with no tick, and no burst afterwards.

questions.question: A handler that takes 3 ms ends with timer.start(10). What is the period?
options: 7 ms
It depends on the timer type only
13 ms: the interval counts from now, which is after the work
10 ms
questions.explanation: In 300 ms the re-armed timer ticked 22 times where 30 periods went by.

questions.question: Why does delay_to_next_ms round up?
options: To avoid a division
To make the delay longer on purpose
Because QTimer takes only even numbers
So the timer never fires early, into a slot that has already been delivered
questions.explanation: A timer that fires a hair early lands in the same slot, and that is not a tick.

questions.question: After a run, what holds for a Ticker?
options: ticks() + missed() equals last_slot()
missed() is always 0
ticks() equals last_slot()
ticks() is the elapsed time in ms
questions.explanation: Every slot up to the last is either a tick or counted as missed.

questions.question: A ramp adds 0.01 per tick. After a 100 ms block it is behind. What is the fix?
options: Use the clock or the slot numbers for the time, and the ticks only for when to look
A faster timer
Block less
Count the ticks twice
questions.explanation: 30 or 31 ticks counted 300 or 310 ms in 400 ms of real time.

questions.question: What does the Ticker not do?
options: Keep the slots in order
Make the event loop real time: a block still costs its slots
Avoid drift from the handler's work
Report skipped slots
questions.explanation: It tells you about a block; a loop that cannot tolerate one needs its own thread.
